diagnostic_evidence.quote: Specifically, our experiments suggest that for any sufficiently large $k$ and $\kappa$, we can find a problem instance for which the backward error of \algne\ after $k$ iterations is at least $\min\{1, \log_{10}(\kappa)/k\}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction states a construction and a lower bound for MINBERR-NE and implies a negative conclusion for all deterministic Krylov methods. The paper only presents empirical observations for MINBERR-NE; no proof of the claimed lower bound is given, and a lower bound for one algorithm does not imply a lower bound for all deterministic Krylov methods.

failure_location.quote: However, we are able to construct a family of hard problem instances for which the \algne\ backward error is at least $\log(\kappa(\A))/k$ after $k$ iterations, suggesting that no deterministic Krylov method can attain truly universal convergence for general systems.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the claim to say that the Small-Outlier family empirically suggests such stagnation for MINBERR-NE, and remove the implication for all deterministic Krylov methods unless a proof is added.
issues.overall_effect: The negative/hardness statement for general linear systems is unsupported and potentially misleading, although the PSD formal results do not depend on it.
issues.title: Introduction overclaims a proven hard-instance lower bound for MINBERR-NE
issues.why_classification: A local wording repair preserves all formal claims and requires no new mathematical content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\Pc_{k-1}$ denote the set of all polynomials $p(x)=c_0+c_1x + \cdots +c_{k-1}x^{k-1}$ of degree at most $k-1$ with real-valued coefficients.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof minimizes over all degree-<k polynomials, but p(A) need not be invertible (for example, p can vanish at an eigenvalue of A). The displayed operator norm containing p(A)^{-1} is therefore not well-defined for all p in the stated minimization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the minimization in the inequality to polynomials p with p(lambda_i) != 0 on the spectrum, or argue directly for the explicitly constructed p, which is positive on [0,1].
issues.overall_effect: As written, the reduction from Krylov minimization to the polynomial approximation problem is not fully justified. The final constructed polynomial is nonsingular on [0,1], so the theorem can be repaired.
issues.title: MINBERR reduction uses inverse of possibly singular p(A)
issues.why_classification: This is a local proof qualification; the advertised O(1/k^2) bound and constructed polynomial remain unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: So it suffices to know that \(h\) is decreasing on \((0,\pi/2]\).

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiating G_l(u)=csc^2(lu)-l^{-2}csc^2(u) gives G_l'(u)=(2/(l^2u^3))(l h(u)-h(lu)), where h(x)=x^3 csc^2(x) cot(x). The source states (2/(l^2u^3))(h(u)-h(lu)), which is algebraically incorrect. The monotonicity conclusion can still be recovered because l h(u)-h(lu) >= 0 when h is decreasing, but the displayed calculation is false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the derivative to (2/(l^2u^3))(l h(u)-h(lu)) and repeat the same decreasing-h argument.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the explicit trigonometric bound, and therefore the proof of the MINBERR rate, contains an invalid calculation step.
issues.title: Incorrect derivative formula in proof of shifted Chebyshev bound
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and does not change the lemma statement or the resulting 3/(k^2-1) bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm declares convergence when the exact Krylov minimizer has backward error below epsilon, but the subsequent inverse iteration only yields an approximate minimizer. The complexity theorem guarantees at most (1+1/2) times the exact minimizer, so the returned iterate can have backward error up to 1.5 epsilon, violating the stated output contract berr < epsilon.

failure_location.quote: if this breaks down (i.e., $\sigma_{\min}(\tilde\T)=\berr_{\A,\b}(\x_k)<\epsilon$), proceed to step 7.

issues.overall_effect: As written, the algorithm's epsilon tolerance contract is not supported by its own approximation analysis; the advertised big-O complexity is unaffected if constants are adjusted.
issues.title: MINBERR stopping tolerance not matched to approximate minimizer guarantee
issues.why_classification: This is a constant-factor tolerance mismatch; a local change preserves the O(1/sqrt epsilon) complexity and all substantive claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, for a $1/2$-relative error ($\Delta = 0.5$), we require $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(n/\delta^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma gives a sufficient iteration count containing an additive constant, an extra ln ln(2/delta) term, and coefficient 1/(2 ln(1+Delta/2)) ~ 2.2407 for Delta=1/2. The simplified bound 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) is not implied by the lemma for general finite k and delta, so the probability guarantee used by the algorithm and theorem is not supported by the cited lemma.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) by the exact sufficient bound from the lemma, or by a larger explicit expression such as C ln(k/delta^2)+C ln ln(1/delta) with a valid constant.
issues.overall_effect: The stated with-probability 1-delta guarantee for the approximate singular vector, and hence for the algorithm's tolerance analysis, is not established as written.
issues.title: Inverse-iteration count 2.23 ln(k/delta^2) does not follow from the stated lemma
issues.why_classification: Only a constant/additive-log correction is needed; the O(log(1/delta)) complexity and high-probability guarantee type are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By combining the $O(1/k^2)$ convergence guarantee from Theorem \ref{t:minberr} with the complexity analysis in Theorem \ref{thm:minberrcost}, we immediately obtain the following.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is stated for all PSD A, but the complexity/probability theorem used in its one-line derivation assumes A is positive definite. For singular PSD systems the Lanczos/inverse-iteration analysis does not apply as written; for example, A=diag(1,0) and b=(0,1)^T gives immediate Lanczos breakdown although the corollary claims an epsilon-backward-error solution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the corollary to A >> 0, or add the singular case using the source's suggested regularization A+eta||A||I and Lemma l:composition, with a matching complexity argument.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised O(n^2/sqrt epsilon) guarantee for the full PSD class is not supported for the singular regime.
issues.title: Corollary extends complexity theorem from A >> 0 to all A >>_ 0 without proof
issues.why_classification: The fix is contained but requires handling a degenerate input class and an extra regularization/complexity argument; simply deleting the singular regime would lose advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Set $\tilde\B_k$ as the bottom $k\times k$ submatrix of $\B_k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The recurrence for d does not correctly test whether the smallest singular value of the bottom bidiagonal matrix tildeB_k is below epsilon. For k=2, take tildeB_2 = [[0.6, 1], [0, 1]] and epsilon=0.5. The algorithm sets d_1=0.36-0.25=0.11, then d_2=0.11*1/(0.11+1)-0.25 < 0, so it declares sigma_min<0.5. In fact sigma_min(tildeB_2)=1, so the test gives a false positive and the algorithm can terminate before the backward-error tolerance is reached.

failure_location.quote: If $d>0$, return to step 2. Else, $\sigma_{\min}(\tilde \B_k)=\berr_{\A,\b}(\x_k)<\epsilon,$ so go to step 7.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the recurrence with a correct test for sigma_min(tildeB_k)<epsilon, e.g. a correct dqds update for the bidiagonal matrix or direct Cholesky/pivot test on tildeB_k^T tildeB_k - epsilon^2 I.
issues.overall_effect: The MINBERR-NE algorithm's stated tolerance contract is unreliable: its convergence detector can incorrectly signal berr < epsilon.
issues.title: MINBERR-NE dqds convergence test is not equivalent to sigma_min < epsilon
issues.why_classification: The failure is local to the nonsymmetric algorithm's stopping test, but it invalidates the algorithm's output guarantee and requires a corrected invariant/test; the PSD results are unaffected.
